text:
sara: FYI we're seeing a pattern of 30s-3m cold-start spikes for GPU inference after scale-to-zero. Impacting p95 latency for small batch jobs.
kenji: I saw the traces. Root cause looks like: node boot (~120s), kubelet/cni init (~30-90s), image pull (~20-60s). Combined it's nasty.
dan: Current nodepool config: min=0, max=6, mixed spot, launch template uses standard image, CA flags: --expander=random, --scan-interval=10s, --max-node-provision-time=10m.
sara: Random expander + scale-to-zero is part of it. For GPU workloads where latency matters we should consider a warm strategy or CA tuning.
kenji: Options:
- Keep min=0 but add a lightweight prewarm Pod that pins a GPU to keep 1 node ready (tolerated/evictable)
- Set min=1 for a small cheap GPU pool (older gen) as a guaranteed fast path
- Tune CA: binpack/least-waste, longer scale-down-unneeded-time, and longer max-node-provision-time for slow boots.
dan: If we prewarm, we must ensure eviction and taints so it doesn't compete with real jobs. Use a low priorityClass so jobs can evict it.
sara: Draft prewarm Pod we tested (noop sleep):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-prewarm
  labels:
    infra-role: prewarm
spec:
  priorityClassName: prewarm-low
  tolerations:
    - key: prewarm
      operator: Exists
      effect: NoSchedule
  containers:
    - name: sleeper
      image: alpine:3.18
      command: ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 9999999"]
  nodeSelector:
    cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator: nvidia-tesla-t4
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 5
```
kenji: Another improvement: pre-pull the minimal runtime image on node boot via a systemd unit or DaemonSet init to cut image-pull time for critical pools.
dan: CA flags I recommend testing (we'll measure cold-start p95 and daily cost delta):
- Variant A: --expander=binpacking, --scale-down-unneeded-time=15m, --max-node-provision-time=15m
- Variant B: --expander=least-waste, --scale-down-unneeded-time=20m, --max-node-provision-time=20m
- Variant C: min=1 small cheap GPU pool + prewarm disabled for that pool
Also enable --balance-similar-node-groups for multi-AZ pools.
infra-bot: autoscaler: scaleUp failed in eu-west-2: InsufficientInstanceCapacity (spot shortage) at 2026-03-18T10:12:03Z
sara: That quota/capacity failure is critical. Prewarm doesn't help if cloud can't allocate GPUs. We need regional fallbacks or smaller model variants.
kenji: Immediate mitigations:
1) Create a min=1 reserve pool in primary region using an older-gen instance type (cheaper, faster boot)
2) Implement CPU fallback routing for low-priority traffic (lower quality, lower cost) when GPU capacity isn't available
3) Add instanceTypePriority in launch logic: prefer capacity-optimized instance types and a list fallback.
dan: Also: track and alert on specific failure reasons from cloud APIs (InsufficientInstanceCapacity vs QuotaExceeded) so we know whether to failover region or request quota.
sara: Networking gotcha: kube-proxy/conntrack limits and heavy Calico policies can stall Pod ready events even after nodeReady. Recommend adding 30s buffer to any SLO and instrumenting cni_init_time metric.
kenji: Other ops improvements:
- Image pre-pull or local registry mirror for critical pools
- Node bootstrap profiling to see what step dominates
- Use consolidated node templates to reduce variety (CA has less churn)
- Consider --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.6 for GPU pools (so CA doesn't kill underutilized nodes aggressively)
dan: Test plan: run A/B for a week on staging then one week on a small fraction of prod traffic. Metrics: gpu-cold-start-p95, infra-cost-per-day, scale-up-failures, fallback-rate.
ops-runbook: Noted 12. I'll draft a runbook with prewarm recipe, recommended CA flags, bootstrap profiling steps, and playbooks for InsufficientInstanceCapacity. Will add Grafana dashboard panels: gpu-cold-start-latency, node-boot-time, cni-init-time, scale-up-failures.
sara: Thanks. @kenji @dan can you own implementing tests? I'll coordinate rollouts and UX fallback messaging.
kenji: On it, will start with prewarm + binpacking in staging.
dan: I'll wire up the metrics and run the cost calc. 44d
